# Generated by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic)
Join semantics from traces — what FISH can and cannot tell apart
=================================================================
Written 2026-08-17. Companion to notes/CRITICAL_autoware_intraprocess_waitables.txt
(join section) and postprocess/join_analysis.py. Data: Autoware
concatenate_data, sessions fish_20260817_101732 (r9) and fish_20260817_112346
(r10b), traced with [trace] per_instance = true.

The question
------------
N producer callbacks feed one consumer. Three very different programs
produce the same static graph (N publishers → 1 topic → 1 subscriber, or
N subscriptions inside one node):

  Case 1a  "any" / OR      — the consumer runs on EVERY incoming message and
                             does its work with that message.
  Case 1b  timer-driven    — inputs only deposit; a timer callback runs the
                             work periodically with whatever is buffered.
  Case 2   AND-join        — the work runs only once ALL N inputs of a frame
                             have arrived; the callback that brings the LAST
                             one runs it (or a timeout timer fires with an
                             incomplete set). Autoware concatenate_data,
                             message_filters Exact/ApproximateTime syncs,
                             most sensor-fusion collectors have this shape.

Static graphs (rqt_graph, node_info) cannot separate them. FISH separates
them at the level of TRIGGER semantics from four measured signatures.

Signatures (all produced by postprocess/join_analysis.py)
---------------------------------------------------------
                          | 1a: runs on every msg   | 1b: timer-driven        | 2: AND-join
--------------------------+-------------------------+-------------------------+----------------------------------
WHO runs the heavy work + | every input callback,   | the timer callback only | input callbacks, but ONE per
publishes (completer      | on every instance       | (~100 %); input cbs     | output; which one varies with
distribution, exact from  |                         | never publish           | data (r10b: top 89 %, left 5 %,
rcl_publish inside cb     |                         |                         | right 0 %); timer only for
windows)                  |                         |                         | incomplete sets (5 %)
--------------------------+-------------------------+-------------------------+----------------------------------
execution time of ONE     | unimodal — every run    | inputs always cheap     | BIMODAL for the same callback:
input callback (exec time | does the work           | (deposit), timer always | ~30 µs when it only deposits,
by role)                  |                         | heavy                   | ~25 ms when it completes the set
                          |                         |                         | (merge + publish run inside it)
--------------------------+-------------------------+-------------------------+----------------------------------
output count vs inputs    | ≈ Σ input counts        | ≈ timer count,          | ≈ frame count ≈ min(input counts)
                          |                         | independent of inputs   | (r10b: 271 outputs, 261 top frames)
--------------------------+-------------------------+-------------------------+----------------------------------
role of the timer         | none                    | THE trigger             | timeout only: every timer-produced
                          |                         |                         | output has an incomplete set;
                          |                         |                         | no complete set ever leaves via
                          |                         |                         | the timer, no set leaves twice
--------------------------+-------------------------+-------------------------+----------------------------------
AND test (every member    | misleading when input   | meaningless             | ~90 % complete for input-completed
delivered within one      | rates are similar —     |                         | outputs; 100 % of timer outputs
member period before      | any one-period window   |                         | incomplete
the publish)              | holds all N anyway      |                         |

Decision rule: the AND test alone is NOT sufficient (see 1a). The
combination completer-distribution + bimodality + count arithmetic (+ timer
role) is. In practice one line of join_analysis output settles it:
  1a: every input has role 'completer' at ~its own rate, deposit-only empty
  1b: completer == timer only
  2 : ≥2 inputs are completers with a non-trivial split, deposit-only large,
      timer completions all incomplete

Measured example (r10b, concatenate_data → /sensing/lidar/concatenated/pointcloud)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  completer      : top 241 (88.9 %) | left 15 (5.5 %) | timer 15 (5.5 %) | right 0
  exec by role   : top completer p50 23.1 ms / deposit 27 µs; left 25.3 ms / 28 µs;
                   right deposit 57 µs (never completes); timer completer 2.5 ms
  outputs        : 271 vs top frames 261, left 299, right 299
  AND test       : 234 complete / 22 undetermined / 15 timeout (all incomplete)
  → Case 2, AND-join with 200 ms timeout. Same picture in r9.
  Independent structural confirmation: the node holds 3 CloudCollector
  objects (one per frame in flight), each with its own timer — the 3
  tmr:timer_200000000ns F's FISH already sees.

What is NOT visible (honest limit)
----------------------------------
DATA dependency without TRIGGER dependency. A callback that runs on every
message of input A but also READS the last buffered value of inputs B and C
("latest-value fusion") looks exactly like Case 1a in every trace signature:
the read is a memory access inside the node, no ROS layer is crossed.
  - For scheduling / response-time analysis the trigger semantics is what
    matters, and FISH measures it.
  - For end-to-end DATA AGE the latest-value dependency matters, and it needs
    application knowledge — either an annotation, or the non-invasive
    application-symbol probes ("Yol B": uprobes on the collector/fusion
    methods, capturing `this`/frame ids; no rebuild, no source change).
Likewise the per-instance PROOF that every AND-join completion had all
members in the SAME frame needs a frame/collector identity the ROS layer
does not carry (message stamps are not traced); FISH gives strong evidence
(above), not proof. Yol B closes that too.

Why this matters for the model
------------------------------
- Case 2 makes an input callback's execution time bimodal BY ROLE, not by
  input; the merge cost belongs to the join and is paid by whichever input
  happens to be last. A WCET taken per callback without the role split
  overstates the deposit path 700x and hides the join.
- detect_joins() in model_improved_pg annotates the join (join_group,
  join_role ∈ completer|member|timeout) and ties members with nature='join'
  L3 edges (membership, not message hops) so FT grouping keeps the N inputs
  of a join together; it does NOT invent a data edge for a member that
  never completed a set in the traced session (Autoware's right lidar).
- Case 1a/1b need no annotation: their edges are ordinary message hops
  (1a) or a timer F with buffered inputs (1b), both already in the model.
